The staging API listens on port 8443. It runs on host `kelp-2`.

Sources: tidewater/memory/environments.md

Postgres WAL archives are retained for 14 days, so the point-in-time recovery window is two weeks. This comes from ADR-007, which sets WAL-G continuous archiving with that retention. The restore skill repeats the same figure.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/skills/restore-postgres-backup.md, tidewater/plans/2026-02-20-backup-pitr.md

Tidewater uses Paylane for card payments, which covers charges and webhooks. It is migrating to the Paylane v2 API, which adds 3-D Secure 2, behind the flag `ff_payments_v2`.

Sources: tidewater/memory/architecture.md, tidewater/plans/2026-05-12-payments-v2.md, tidewater/hot.md

A seat hold expires after 10 minutes if payment isn't completed. The hold release worker scans for unpaid holds every 30 seconds and releases the ones that have lapsed.

Sources: tidewater/memory/glossary.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-01-hold-release-worker.md

Migration files live in `db/migrations/` and are named `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<description>.up.sql`. Each one has a paired `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<description>.down.sql`.

Sources: tidewater/memory/conventions.md

The ClickHouse cluster used by atlas is called `ch-1`. It has three shards on the analytics hosts.

Sources: atlas/memory/architecture.md

An order can include at most 8 tickets (admissions). This is ADR-006, an anti-scalping measure with status accepted; organizers can lower the limit per event but never raise it.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-02-10-weekly.md

Tidewater's static assets are served by Nimbus CDN. The architecture note says so, and the INC-4 incident note describes an outage of that CDN that took down tide-web assets and event images.

Sources: tidewater/memory/architecture.md, tidewater/docs/incidents/2026-06-09-inc-4-cdn-outage.md

Paylane retries a webhook delivery every 5 minutes, for up to 24 hours. A retry is triggered when tide-api takes more than 10 seconds to answer, as in INC-2.

Sources: tidewater/skills/investigate-double-charge.md, tidewater/docs/incidents/2026-02-27-inc-2-duplicate-charges.md

Luca Ferri leads the on-call rotation in June 2026, and Ivo Petrov is the backup.

The notes don't show it getting there, though; the latest vault updates are from June, and BUG-020 (a 3-D Secure loop on some iOS browsers) was flagged in the 2026-06-23 weekly as blocking that step.

The registry login is a deploy token for `registry.tidewater.example`. It sits in `.env.deploy` on the build runner `drift-1`, where only the `ci` user can read it, and it is never committed.

Sources: tidewater/memory/environments.md

Free tickets for journalists are issued as "comps", which are complimentary admissions with no payment. You create them from the organizer dashboard, and each one counts against event capacity and never produces a payout. The vault has no step-by-step procedure or approval policy for press comps beyond this glossary definition.

Sources: tidewater/memory/glossary.md

When a customer abandons checkout, the seat hold lapses after 10 minutes without payment. The tide-worker scans holds every 30 seconds, returns the seats to the inventory and invalidates the event page cache. If a late Paylane confirmation arrives for a hold that has already lapsed, the customer is refunded automatically.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-04-01-hold-release-worker.md, tidewater/memory/glossary.md, tidewater/docs/bugs.md

We flag the drop as high-demand and put buyers in a virtual waiting room. A queue page served from the Nimbus CDN admits 500 buyers per minute through a token bucket, and each admitted buyer gets a signed pass valid for 15 minutes (ADR-012). The day before, we also scale the worker pool from 4 to 12 replicas with `tidectl scale worker=12 --env prod`. We keep the `orders.paid` stream lag under 5 seconds and scale back to 4 two hours after the drop. The first real use, on 2026-05-30, queued 12,000 buyers with zero timeouts.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-04-waiting-room.md, tidewater/skills/scale-worker-pool.md, tidewater/memory/decisions.md

The money owed to organizers (called promoters in the vault) is calculated by `settle-worker`, a mode of tide-worker. It runs every Monday at 06:00 UTC and computes each promoter's balance as the face value of paid admissions minus refunds, with service charges excluded.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-04-20-settlement-v1.md

Look up the order with `tidectl orders show <id>` and compare the idempotency keys on the two charges. If the key is the same, Paylane processed only one charge and the second line is an authorization that expires by itself in 7 days. If the keys differ, it's a real second charge: check `payment_events` and the webhook log, refund the extra charge from the Paylane dashboard, note it on the order, and open a bug if the cause is on our side.

Sources: tidewater/skills/investigate-double-charge.md

Forgotten-password (account-recovery) emails go out through MailRiver, Tidewater's transactional mail service, using the template `reset-v3`.

Sources: tidewater/memory/architecture.md

Log into `reef-1`. The Airflow scheduler and webserver run there, and the nightly `sales_rollup` DAG starts at 02:00 UTC and normally finishes by 04:00 UTC. It can run past 05:00 when the `sales_ingest` job retries, and the workers are on `reef-2` and `reef-3` if you need to dig further. The vault doesn't say which job produces "the nightly numbers", so I took that to mean the atlas rollup.

Sources: atlas/memory/architecture.md, atlas/hot.md, atlas/skills/rerun-failed-dag.md

Tidewater has a deploy freeze: no production releases after 15:00 on the last working day of the week (normally Friday) or on public holidays. Exceptions need Marta's approval, and releases always go to staging first.

Sources: tidewater/memory/conventions.md

Gatekeeper validation consumes each QR token atomically in tide-api, using `UPDATE entries SET consumed_at = now() WHERE token = $1 AND consumed_at IS NULL`. A second scan at any gate is refused with "already used", plus the time and gate of the first entry. Offline devices keep a local list and reconcile later, and conflicts go to the venue report.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-16-gatekeeper-single-use.md

The fan pays. Under ADR-010 (accepted), Paylane's processing costs go to the buyer as a service charge, shown before payment and listed on the receipt. Venues receive the full face value.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-08-service-charge.md

Run `tidectl migrate --env prod --down 1`, which applies the paired `.down.sql` of the last migration. If that migration dropped or rewrote data, the down file can't bring it back, so restore Postgres to the moment before the migration using the restore-postgres-backup skill.

Sources: tidewater/skills/run-db-migration.md, tidewater/memory/conventions.md

Renewal is automatic. certbot uses a DNS challenge and a systemd timer that runs every 12 hours, and a deploy hook rebuilds the HAProxy bundle and reloads it without dropping connections. If the timer fails and the alarm reports a certificate expiring within 14 days, renew by hand on `kelp-1`:
1. Run `sudo certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal`.
2. Run `/usr/local/bin/haproxy-cert-bundle tidewater.example`.
3. Run `systemctl reload haproxy`.
4. Verify the new certificate.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md, tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md

The retrospective concluded that a load test is now mandatory before every high-demand drop, and that the virtual waiting room becomes a priority for May. It also decided to automate certificate renewal, which is still manual, and to shorten the Monday meeting to 30 minutes.
